transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble at work lately. Well, I mean, it's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really do try to be a good employee. I work in meat processing, and... I keep starting the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and then I just... somehow I leave out the very last parts. 

I don't know why I do it, especially when I know my job depends on finishing everything correctly. I really want to do it right, I promise I'm trying. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing I'm supposed to talk about here?
Have you had this kind of difficulty finishing tasks since childhood?

Um, yeah... I think so. I mean, I was always a really good student, I promise! But... well, my mom actually still has some of my old elementary school report cards, like from around fourth grade. And they usually said I was bright—which was really nice of them to say!—but... they also mentioned that I needed constant reminders to finish my classwork and actually turn in my homework. 

It's a little embarrassing to look back on. I remember I would understand the lessons perfectly fine, but I'd somehow just miss chunks of the instructions... unless the teacher was standing right next to me to keep me on track. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was just ignoring them, because I really wasn't trying to be difficult or anything. Does that help? Is that the kind of childhood stuff you're looking for?
Do you find yourself having unwanted, intrusive thoughts that are hard to stop?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I do. I mean, my mind definitely wanders a lot—probably way more than it should, honestly! But it's not really like... bad or scary thoughts forcing their way in, if that makes sense? 

It's more like my brain just kind of floats away from what I'm doing, or I just lose my train of thought completely. I don't really have thoughts that I'm actively trying to stop or push away, I just kind of... space out. I hope it's okay that I don't have that! Am I answering that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you also find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you need to sit still?

Oh, um... no, actually. I don't really do that. I'm actually pretty good at sitting still, I promise! 

I don't really bounce my leg or feel like I need to get up and walk around or anything. When I'm sitting, I'm usually just... well, sitting perfectly quiet. Maybe my mind is wandering a bit too much, like I mentioned, but my body is completely still. 

I hope that's okay? I know sometimes people expect you to be really hyper or bouncy when you talk about focusing issues, and I really don't want to confuse things or give you the wrong answers. Is it alright that I don't have that restless feeling? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Do you have similar trouble staying focused or finishing things in other parts of your life, like at home or in social situations?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? But it's really not that bad, I promise! I mean, at work—I'm a meat processor—I try really, really hard to stay on top of things because obviously, you have to be careful. Sometimes I might take a little longer to finish a batch than the others, or I might need someone to repeat an order, but I always get it done! 

At home, um... maybe I leave a few chores half-finished sometimes? Like, I'll start folding laundry and then get distracted by the dishes, and then maybe neither gets totally finished right away. But I always go back to it eventually! And with my friends, I really try to listen, I do. Sometimes I might drift off for a second if the story is really long, but I try so hard to nod and smile so they don't feel bad. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a mess or a bad friend. I really do try my best to keep it all together. Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do these attention and finishing problems cause real difficulties in your daily life?

Oh, um... well, I mean... I guess it does cause some issues, but I really don't want to make it sound like I'm incapable or anything! I try so, so hard to do everything right. 

But, um... at work, it has gotten a little... complicated. I actually had to have some formal retraining meetings recently, which was really embarrassing. I felt so bad taking up my manager's time! And sometimes my coworkers have to step in and cover parts of my duties when I fall behind. They're super nice about it, but I just hate being a burden to them. 

I'm just really scared that they're going to move me off the line, or... or even fire me. Working with meat processing, you have to be so careful, and I just feel like I'm becoming a safety concern instead of the reliable worker I want to be. I really don't want to be a problem for anyone! 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee. I really do care about my job and try my absolute best every single day. Is it okay that I admitted that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's a little embarrassing.
